summary: V3-08 repair accepted. The trusted finalizer run 35563950090 failed at step 7 'Android API 35 install, launch and golden path' (the emulator E2E step that has failed 16 consecutive dispatched finalizer runs while all other gates pass). The candidate repairs the concrete E2E blocker: after a force-stop + relaunch (crash detector or stuck detector), the relaunched app needs a fresh cold-start window (documented worst case 240s), but the previous cold-start grace period (COLD_START_GRACE_MS, tied to waitStart) has already elapsed, so the stuck-app detector immediately counts empty dumps against the fresh cold start and force-stops again — an infinite kill loop. The fix adds FORCE_STOP_RECOVERY_MS = 300s: every force-stop path (APP CRASHED pidof-empty, APP CRASHED pidof-exit-1, APP STUCK) records globalThis._lastForceStopTime = Date.now(), and stuck detection only increments consecutiveEmptyMatchCount once 300s have elapsed since the last force-stop, with 'FORCE-STOP RECOVERY' diagnostic logging. A new contract test guards the constant, the tracking variable, all three force-stop paths, the recovery check and the logging. The delta is confined to scripts/e2e-android.js (+39/-2) and its contract test (+25); no product code (src/, app/), governance, directives, workflows or release state were touched, so V3-01..V3-07 invariants cannot regress. Trusted verification exit code is 0 (typecheck PASS, 453/453 tests PASS in 22 suites, privacy 71/71 PASS, cost 21/21 PASS, expo export android PASS, prebuild PASS, assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 17m25s). Independent re-runs confirm typecheck, 453 tests, privacy 71, cost 21, node --check and bash -n all pass. A 9-scenario simulation of the waitFor logic confirms: healthy 240s/350s cold starts are never force-stopped; a healthy 550s cold start gets exactly one force-stop then recovers (previously killed again -> timeout); a genuinely stuck app is still detected and bounded by the waitFor timeout; a crash mid-path followed by a healthy 240s cold start recovers without a kill loop; normal waits are unaffected. Limitation documented: the raw step-7 logs of run 35563950090 return HTTP 403 without admin rights and no factory token is present in this environment, but the public API confirms the failure point (step 7, emulator E2E) and the fix directly targets that step's stuck-app detector kill-loop hypothesis, which the previous grace-period fix did not cover.

findings.path: scripts/e2e-android.js (stuck-app detector kill loop after force-stop) — repaired
findings.problem: After a force-stop + relaunch (crash detector or stuck detector), the relaunched app needs a fresh cold-start window (documented worst case 240s on API 35 x86_64), but the cold-start grace period added in the previous cycle is tied to waitStart and has already elapsed. The stuck-app detector therefore immediately counts empty dumps against the fresh cold start (STUCK_APP_THRESHOLD=4 dumps = 2-4 min) and force-stops again, resetting the cold start each cycle — an infinite kill loop that fails the finalizer emulator E2E step. Run 35563950090 failed at exactly this step (step 7), the 16th consecutive dispatched finalizer failure at the same step.

Candidate fix: FORCE_STOP_RECOVERY_MS=300_000; globalThis._lastForceStopTime = Date.now() recorded at every force-stop path (APP CRASHED pidof-empty line 426, APP CRASHED pidof-exit-1 line 444, APP STUCK line 493); stuck detection increments consecutiveEmptyMatchCount only when sinceLastForceStop >= FORCE_STOP_RECOVERY_MS (line 480); 'FORCE-STOP RECOVERY' diagnostic logging. Simulation (9 scenarios): healthy 550s cold start -> 1 force-stop then found at 555s (previously second force-stop at ~660s > 600s timeout); crash mid-path + healthy 240s cold start -> found, no kill loop; genuinely stuck app -> still force-stopped, bounded by timeout.
